facts.text: `dio` sets `use_direct_io` in the model loader and turns `use_mmap` off. The only code that opens the GGUF with `O_DIRECT` is guarded by `#ifdef __linux__`; the Windows variant reports direct I/O as available; the remaining POSIX branch (macOS) opens a normal buffered `FILE*` and its `has_direct_io()` is `fd != -1 && alignment > 1`, which is false there.
Result on macOS: `dio` is accepted, logs `load_mode = dio`, and loads like `none` (weights copied into host-allocated buffers), with no warning.

Lazy tensors are mapped even when the load mode is not `mmap`: the loader builds file mappings when `use_mmap || lazy.any()`. Only the lazy tensors are served from the mapping; the rest follow the chosen load mode.
`lazy_read::add` skips a tensor in `off` mode, skips tensors of 4 GiB or less unless mode is `on`, and, if the build has no mmap support, logs that the tensor "is loaded into RAM in full".
mlock never pins a lazy tensor, because that would fault the whole table in.

PR 20834 (taronaeo, opened 2026-03-21) folded `--mlock`, `--mmap` and `--direct-io` into one enum, marking the old flags deprecated first. A reviewer rejected making DirectIO the automatic default on GPU builds because it had been tried before and failed on a "not insignificant number of configurations".
PR 26135 (opened 2026-07-26, merged) corrected the refactor's regression (issue 26110): `-lm mlock` now means lock without mmap; `-lm mmap+mlock` means lock with mmap.
PR 28334 (opened 2026-09-03, same author) removes the deprecated flag spellings from the argument parser as "the final cleanup".
The lazy flag was first proposed as `--tensor-read-lazy`; master and the installed Ollama-bundled build both list `-lzm, --lazy-mode` with env `LLAMA_ARG_LAZY_MODE`.
`-lm dio` on a Mac silently degrades to `none`: higher RSS and slower load than mmap, and no page-cache bypass. [asserted by source reading and local test below]
`llama_prefetch` exists only for Linux and Windows, so on macOS there is no prefetch of mapped ranges, and the "skip prefetch" half of lazy mode has nothing to skip.

`--load-mode mlock` after PR 26135 no longer enables mmap, so it behaves like the old `--no-mmap --mlock` pair; before it, `mlock` meant mmap plus mlock and a user reported being killed for out-of-memory.
On macOS `mlock` failures print a hint naming `vm.user_wire_limit`, `vm.global_user_wire_limit`, `vm.global_no_user_wire_amount` and `ulimit -l`.
Which PR renamed `--tensor-read-lazy` to `--lazy-mode`.
Whether a macOS direct-read path (`F_NOCACHE`) is planned for `dio`; none found in source.
Measured effect of `--lazy-mode on` on a Mac with a table above 4 GiB (only gemma-4 E4B numbers exist).
The argument table defines `-lm, --load-mode` with values auto, none, mmap, mlock, mmap+mlock and dio, and env `LLAMA_ARG_LOAD_MODE`; `dio` is described as "use DirectIO if available".
The argument table defines `-lzm, --lazy-mode` with values on, auto, off, env `LLAMA_ARG_LAZY_MODE`, where `on` requires mmap and `auto` means on only for tensors larger than 4 GiB.
The model loader sets `use_mmap` for auto, mmap and mmap+mlock, and sets `use_direct_io` only for `dio`.
`llama_file` opens with `O_RDONLY | O_DIRECT` only inside `#ifdef __linux__`.
In the POSIX `llama_file` implementation, `has_direct_io()` returns `fd != -1 && alignment > 1`, so it is false when no `O_DIRECT` descriptor was opened.
`llama_prefetch` is compiled only for `__linux__` or Windows 8 and later.
The macOS mlock failure hint names `vm.user_wire_limit`, `vm.global_user_wire_limit`, `vm.global_no_user_wire_amount` and `ulimit -l`.
On Linux the PR 20834 debug trace shows `llama_model_loader: direct I/O is enabled, disabling mmap` and a single aligned read path (`alignment=4096`) in `dio` mode.

PR 20834 states it "overhauls the three separate loading modes (mlock, mmap, and direct-io) into one single -lm/--load-mode option" and marks `--mlock`, `--mmap`, `--direct-io` and their negative forms deprecated.

A reviewer on PR 20834 wrote that defaulting to DirectIO "was a bad idea" because it "seems to fail on a not insignificant number of configurations", and suggested disabling mmap by default on GPU builds instead.
The PR 20834 author confirmed that `--load-mode none` equals the old `--no-mmap`.
PR 26135 redefines `-lm mlock` as memory-lock only, without mmap, and `-lm mmap+mlock` as lock with mmap, to fix issue 26110.
RESOLVES the open question in llama-cpp-metal-backend-on-mac.md about `--load-mode mlock` semantics after regression 26110: after PR 26135, `mlock` does not map the file.
PR 28334 (opened 2026-09-03) removes the `--mmap`, `--mlock` and `--direct-io` spellings from the argument parser as the final cleanup of the refactor.
`lazy_read::add` returns false for `off`, returns false when the tensor is 4 GiB or smaller unless mode is `on`, and warns that the tensor "is loaded into RAM in full" when mmap is unsupported.
The loader skips mlock growth for lazy tensors, with the comment that locking one "would fault all of it in, which is what lazy avoids".
Ollama's launcher passes `--load-mode dio` only on Linux with an integrated CUDA or ROCm GPU, `--load-mode none` when `use_mmap` is false, and no lazy-mode flag at all.

Measured on this Mac (macOS arm64, Metal, the Ollama 0.34.4 Homebrew llama-server, build 11081 commit 161755f29, 274 MB GGUF): `-lm auto` logs `load_mode = mmap` with `CPU_Mapped 44.72 MiB` and `MTL0_Mapped 260.86 MiB`.
Measured on the same Mac and build: `-lm dio` logs `load_mode = dio` and non-mapped buffers `CPU 44.72 MiB` and `MTL0 216.15 MiB`, identical to `-lm none`, with no direct-I/O warning.
The same installed build prints `-lm, --load-mode` and `-lzm, --lazy-mode` in `--help`, with the same help text as master.
Inference: `dio` on macOS has no benefit over `none` and should not be recommended; use `auto` (mmap) for fully resident models and `none` only to avoid mapped-span accounting.
CONTRADICTS: llama-cpp-lazy-mode-lazy-tensor-reading-of-overs.md, which treats `--tensor-read-lazy` versus `--lazy-mode` as unresolved: the current argument table has only `--lazy-mode`/`-lzm`.

CONTRADICTS: llama-cpp-lazy-mode-lazy-tensor-reading-of-overs.md ("with mmap off there is nothing to read lazily"): `init_mappings` creates mappings when `use_mmap || lazy.any()`, with the comment that this keeps lazy reading usable "even when --load-mode is not set to mmap".
